title: Topological band structure of excitons in octochlore KTb$_{3}$F$_{10}$: an analog of the Luttinger Semimetal
authors: Olivier Demortier, Françoise Damay, Paul McClarty, Stéphane Raymond, Jacques Ollivier, Sylvain Petit
abstract: Understanding the symmetry and topology of band structures in crystalline solids has been among the defining themes of a generation of condensed matter physicists, with implications across many different platforms including electronic bands, photonic crystals, phonons and magnetic excitations. In the latter systems, there is usually magnetic long-range order and time reversal symmetry breaking. Here we further enrich the possible band structures available to magnetic systems by examining dispersive crystal field excitations above a ground state that is a simple product of singlets. In these systems, there is an interplay of magnetic interactions and band topology with both crystal and time reversal symmetries. Using high-resolution neutron spectroscopy we reveal the dispersion relations of bosonic excitons in KTb$_{3}$F$_{10}$, an experimental realization of the octochlore lattice. We show that there are pinch point features in the scattering intensity. The dominant coupling in this system is the long-range magnetostatic dipolar interaction, whose singularity at the zone center is passed onto the scattering intensity. However, the pinch points survive when the range of the dipoles is truncated to finite shell number in the form of a three-band quadratic band touching protected by cubic symmetry. This model, which is related to the Luttinger semi-metal, provides a general long wavelength model for the emergence of pinch point scattering intensity encompassing also the true long-range dipolar model.
summary: This paper investigates the topological band structure of magnetic excitons in $	ext{KTb}_3	ext{F}_{10}$ using inelastic neutron scattering. By analyzing the observed 'pinch point' singularities, the authors demonstrate that the physics can be accurately modeled by a quadratic band touching Hamiltonian analogous to a Luttinger semi-metal. This provides a general theoretical framework for understanding topological features in magnetic materials.
main_problem: The study aims to understand the symmetry and topology of band structures in crystalline solids, specifically extending this analysis to magnetic excitations in insulating magnets.
main_result: The research reveals unambiguous pinch point features in the exciton dispersion, which are shown to be a generic consequence of a quadratic band touching model related to the Luttinger semi-metal.
method: The study combines high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering (INS) experiments with theoretical modeling using Crystal Field Excitations (CEF) and long-range dipolar Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The physical system is $	ext{KTb}_3	ext{F}_{10}$, an octochlore lattice exhibiting magnetic excitations. The theoretical model involves the long-range magnetostatic dipolar interaction, which is effectively described by a quadratic band touching point Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Dispersive bosonic excitons, 'pinch point features' in the scattering intensity, and spectral weight anomalies observed in iso-energy maps.
important_parameters: Low temperature (1.5 K to 25 K), the wavevector $\mathbf{Q}=400$, and the truncation range of the dipolar interaction.
main_assumptions: The dominant coupling mechanism is assumed to be the long-range magnetostatic dipolar interaction, and the physics is captured by a minimal quadratic touching point model.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate experimental excitation spectra and calculated iso-E maps, clearly showing the characteristic pinched structures and their dependence on energy and scattering plane.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the general problem of band topology in magnets, presenting experimental INS data showing anomalies, theoretically modeling the system using dipole-dipole interactions, and finally demonstrating that a simplified quadratic model successfully reproduces the observed topological features.
why_interesting: The connection drawn between the topological features (pinch points) in magnetic excitations and the Luttinger semi-metal provides a general, symmetry-protected model applicable to various magnetic systems, which is relevant for understanding emergent quantum states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Dispersions. Experimental excitation spectra (left panel) of KTb3F10 at 1.5 K (IN5@ILL) and calculations (right panel) based on a CEF + long-range dipolar Hamiltonian, for various directions of the reciprocal space (a)-(d), respectively [h00]∗, [4k0]∗, [hh1]∗, and [hh4]∗. The insets in the right panels show the corresponding calculated polarization of the modes (i.e., parallel to [h00]∗(Pa, in blue), [0k0]∗(Pb, in green) or [00l]∗(Pc, in red)). Black arrows indicate anomalies in the spectral weight.

FIG. 2. Maps and pinch points. Symmetrized experimental (left panel) iso-E maps (integrated over 0.1 meV)) of the excitation spectra of KTb3F10 at 1.5 K, in the [h00]∗−[0k0]∗(a-b) and [hh0]∗−[00l]∗scattering planes (IN5@ILL). The right panels show the corresponding calculated iso-E maps considering a Hamiltonian taking into account the CEF along with long-range dipole- dipole interactions.
FIG. 3. Zoomed-in iso-E Maps. Zoomed-in iso-E calculations around the pinched motives at Q400, for E = 2.7 meV (a) and 3 meV (b). The corresponding polarization of the modes is shown on the right.

FIG. 4. Truncating the dipolar interaction. Spectral weight calculated using the microscopic model in the immediate vicinity of the zone center Q = 400 zone, in the [h00]∗and [0k0]∗directions, by evaluating the dipole interaction as a finite sum truncated beyond a certain distance d (in ˚A).
